title: NASA Saturn satellite sheet: Titan (VI) mass 1,345.5×10^20 kg, radius 2,575 km
summary: The Saturn satellite fact sheet lists Titan (VI) at mass 1,345.5 × 10^20 kg and radius 2,575 km.
body: NASA's Saturn satellite fact sheet lists Titan (VI) with mass 1,345.5 × 10^20 kg, radius 2,575 km, mean density 1880 kg/m^3, and visual geometric albedo 0.22. Orbital parameters on the same sheet: Semi-major axis (10 3 km) = 1,221.87; Semi-major axis (Saturnian Radii) = 20.273; Orbital Period* (days) = 15.945421; Rotation Period (days) = S; Inclination (degrees) = 0.33; Eccentricity = 0.0292. These are the cells printed on the sheet. The sheet does not say, on this row, which cells are a spacecraft measurement and which are an estimate. The sheet says R indicates retrograde motion, and S indicates synchronous rotation, the rotation period equal to the orbital period. Author of the sheet: Dr. David R. Williams, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center. Last Updated line: 22 July 2025.
